J2.text: The compiler already reports an ambiguous bare constructor at the use site ('constructor Low is ambiguous: A, B all have it; write A.Low') and resolves a bare name from the expected type (const y: B = Low compiles).

J3.text: A local named like a constructor hides it silently: in shadow.nra `const Low = 5` makes `Low` the int. It errors only because the types differ; with a matching type it would compile with a different meaning.

J4.text: D2: syntax follows TypeScript, and 'the same text never means two different things'. TypeScript enum members are always written Color.Red.

J5.text: Prior art: Rust requires Enum::Variant unless `use Enum::*`, and re-exports Some/None/Ok/Err bare in its prelude. Swift allows `.teacher` when the type is known. OCaml, Haskell and Gleam use bare constructors; Gleam imports them by name. TypeScript and Kotlin qualify.

evidence.source: Rust reference (paths, prelude), Swift book (implicit member expressions), Gleam tour (imports), TS handbook (enums)
